channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's economic growth driven by $160 billion in foreign investment over decade
item.description: Uzbekistan has attracted $160 billion in foreign investment over the past ten years, leading to a 2.5-fold increase in economic volume. This investment has funded 2,163 major industrial projects totaling $76 billion and created nearly 6 million jobs, according to state media.

item.title: Samarkand to host 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians in September
item.description: Samarkand will host the 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians of the Inter-Parliamentary Union from September 4-6. The event is expected to draw nearly 300 delegates from 183 countries and 15 international organizations, focusing on youth rights and empowerment.

item.title: Uzbek-Chinese joint venture celebrates Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary
item.description: The joint venture "Asia Trans Gas" held events to mark Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary, uniting Uzbek and Chinese employees. The company highlights the strength of cooperation between Uzbekistan and China, particularly in energy, construction, mining, and logistics, emphasizing human interaction and mutual respect.

item.title: Identities of Two Climbers Who Died on Peak Koromdu Identified
item.description: The identities of two climbers who perished on Peak Koromdu have been confirmed by relatives. The deceased are Maxim Polyansky, 43, from Belarus, and Sergey Rubtsov, 37, from Lithuania. A third group member, 60-year-old Belarusian Nikolay Sviridov, remains missing. Poor weather conditions hampered initial search efforts.

item.title: Special app developed for volunteers of 2026 World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A dedicated Volunteer app has been created for the 6th World Nomad Games, scheduled for August 31 to September 6, 2026, in Kyrgyzstan. Developed by the Digital Technologies Center, the app will assist volunteers with navigation, event information, and communication with city services.

item.title: Tashkent's Fonon jewelry factory put up for sale for 316.7 billion soums
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Assets Management Agency has put up for open auction the state's 100% stake in Gold Moon Tashkent, the owner of the Fonon jewelry factory in Tashkent. The starting price for the asset is 316.67 billion soums, with auctions scheduled for September 28.

item.title: Stepfather sentenced to 23 years for killing 15-year-old stepson in Zhitikara
item.description: A stepfather in Zhitikara, Kostanay region, has been sentenced to 23 years in prison for fatally stabbing his 15-year-old stepson. The incident occurred during a family conflict after drinking alcohol, where the man also attempted to attack the boy's mother.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Confirms No Citizens Among Missing in China Mudslide
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that no Kyrgyz citizens are among the killed or missing following a mudslide in Tibet, China. The disaster, triggered by a collapse of ice and soil, also affected Nepal. Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with hundreds reported missing in Tibet and Nepal, including foreign nationals.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened Over Illegal Pasture Distribution in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Kyrgyzstan's Kochkor district has opened a criminal case for abuse of power after officials illegally transferred 0.7 hectares of state pastureland for private housing construction. The land was allocated to two residents of the Ak-Kiya village in 2023. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan checks border guards' readiness for SCO Summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Border Service Chairman inspected border guards at Manas Airport and border crossings to ensure readiness for the upcoming SCO Summit and World Nomad Games. He reviewed patrol organization, checkpoint operations, and discipline, emphasizing the need for clear and responsible duty performance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Airports Reduce Tariffs for Handling Imported Livestock
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced reduced tariffs at international airports for handling imported livestock. Uzbekistan Airports company offers special preferential rates for processing cattle, sheep, and goats arriving by air. These new conditions aim to lower costs for entrepreneurs importing agricultural animals, making air transport more accessible. The measures cover key operations like unloading and temporary storage.

item.title: Kazakh citizen missing in Nepal amid severe flooding, MFA confirms
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is searching for a citizen missing in Nepal following severe floods. The woman was reportedly part of a tourist group that crossed into China from Nepal. Diplomatic efforts are underway with local authorities to locate her.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Bukhara and Khorezm pledge to eradicate poverty and unemployment by 2026
item.description: The hokimiyats of Bukhara and Khorezm regions in Uzbekistan have announced their intention to completely eliminate poverty and unemployment by the end of 2026. These pledges were made during a ceremony attended by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Bukhara's governor stated that poverty and unemployment would be eradicated by year-end, citing unprecedented development rates for the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Som Strengthens Against Dollar Despite Rising Trade Deficit
item.description: Uzbekistan's national currency, the Som, has unexpectedly strengthened by 7.3% against the US Dollar since June of last year, defying a significant increase in the trade deficit. The trade deficit reached $9.3 billion in the first half of 2026, more than doubling from the previous year. Economists explain that trade deficit is not the sole factor influencing currency exchange rates, with remittances and investments also playing a role.

item.title: Professor detained in Astana on espionage charges; university and authorities silent
item.description: An Uzbek national, Ikboljon Koraboev, a professor of international relations at Maqsut Narikbayev University in Astana, was reportedly detained on July 3 on suspicion of espionage. The university stated he is no longer employed there and declined further comment. Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry and National Security Committee have not provided details.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan border guards' readiness checked ahead of SCO and WIC summits
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's State Border Service, Abdikarim Alimbaev, assessed border guards' readiness at Manas International Airport and several checkpoints. He reviewed service organization, checkpoint operations, and discipline, emphasizing the need for responsible duty performance. The World Nomad Games are set for August 31-September 6, 2026, and the SCO summit is planned for August 31-September 1.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Liquidation of Tunduk OJSC for Digitalization Policy
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has signed a decree to liquidate Tunduk OJSC, aiming to advance a unified state policy in digitalization. The Presidential Affairs Department is tasked with overseeing the liquidation process. Tunduk's functions, assets, and resources will be transferred to the Kyzmat state institution. The president also amended a previous decree, removing Tunduk OJSC from the list of sole suppliers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's State Investment in Construction Exceeds 76 Billion Som
item.description: In January-July 2026, Kyrgyzstan's total construction output reached 245 billion som, 1.6 times higher than the previous year. State investment in construction amounted to 76.7 billion som, a 1.7-fold increase. Domestic sources accounted for 82.4% of capital investments. Foreign direct investment saw a significant surge of 15.3 times, reaching 32.86 billion som.

item.title: Kazakhmys invests 2.7 billion tenge in safety at Zhomart mine
item.description: Kazakhmys has invested 2.7 billion tenge in industrial safety measures at its Zhomart mine. The investment focuses on enhancing underground air quality control, equipping machinery with methane sensors, and modernizing ventilation systems. These upgrades aim to improve safety for the approximately 1,200 workers at the mine, which extracts about 3.8 million tons of ore annually.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's average wage nears $615, financial sector leads with over 100,000 soms
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's average monthly wage reached 53,759 soms in the first half of 2026, a 27.5% increase from the previous year, equivalent to $614.8. The financial and mining sectors reported the highest average wages, exceeding 100,000 soms and 91,000 soms respectively. Bishkek recorded the highest wages in the public sector.

item.title: Average salaries in Kyrgyzstan exceed 53,000 soms in first half of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's average monthly nominal wage reached 53,759 soms in the first half of 2026, a 27.5 percent increase from the previous year. The real wage grew by 15.3 percent. Wages in financial intermediation and insurance averaged over 100,000 soms.

item.title: Kazakhstan Investigates Gasoline Quality Amidst Consumer Complaints About AI-95 and AI-98
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Trade is investigating the quality of AI-95 and AI-98 gasoline following consumer complaints. The probe will examine the entire fuel supply chain, from the Pavlodar Petrochemical Plant (PNHZ) to gas stations. Specific attention will be given to gasoline with additives from Sinoil, QazaqOil, and Helios brands. Results are expected within a week.

item.title: Fruit and berry exports from Kyrgyzstan to Russia's Kirov region doubled
item.description: Fruit and berry exports from Kyrgyzstan to Russia's Kirov region have doubled, according to Rosselkhoznadzor. Between January 1 and August 25, 50.7 tons of produce, including raspberries, strawberries, and cherries, were imported, a 1.9-fold increase compared to the same period last year. No quarantine pests were found in the shipments. Favorable weather, stable logistics, and competitive pricing contributed to the export growth.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's tire exports to Russia surged by nearly 38 times in H1 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's tire exports to Russia increased by almost 38 times in the first six months of 2026, according to the National Statistical Committee. The country supplied 44,300 tires worth $1.562 million to Russia during this period. Russia accounted for 94.9% of Kyrgyzstan's total tire exports of 46,670 units.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's tire exports to Russia surge by nearly 38 times
item.description: Kyrgyzstan significantly increased its tire exports to Russia by almost 38 times in the first six months of the year. The country supplied 44,300 tires valued at $1.562 million to the Russian Federation. Russia accounts for 94.9% of Kyrgyzstan's total tire exports during this period.

item.title: Nepal flood death toll surpasses 177, over 1300 missing
item.description: A flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 has left over 1300 people missing, including at least 700 foreign nationals. More than 177 deaths have been confirmed. The disaster destroyed critical infrastructure, hindering rescue efforts. The flood was caused by a glacial lake outburst, according to the USGS.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's berry exports to Russia's Kirov region double
item.description: Berry exports from Kyrgyzstan to Russia's Kirov region have doubled in the first eight months of 2026, reaching 50.7 tons. This increase is attributed to favorable weather conditions in Kyrgyzstan, more stable and cheaper logistics, and competitive pricing by Kyrgyz producers. No quarantine pests were found in the shipments.

item.title: Berry shipments from Kyrgyzstan to Russia's Kirov region double
item.description: Berry shipments from Kyrgyzstan to Russia's Kirov region have doubled in volume. Between January 1 and August 25, 50.7 tons of berries were imported, a 1.9-fold increase compared to the same period last year. Favorable weather, stable logistics, and competitive pricing contributed to this growth.

item.title: Kazakhstan's New Parliament: Meritocracy Under Party Control and Opposition's Role
item.description: Kazakhstan's new parliament, the Kurultai, will hold its first session on August 28, with all five parties that passed the five percent threshold publishing their final deputy lists. President Tokayev will preside over the oath-taking ceremony. Political analyst Ilyas Baktygaliyev suggests the Kurultai's composition appears meritocratic, despite the dominant party holding 110 out of 145 seats.

item.title: Uzbekistan Grants Citizenship to 264 Individuals Under Presidential Decree
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a decree granting citizenship to 264 individuals on the occasion of Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary. Among those granted citizenship is Khursanoy Jumaboeva, who was born in Tajikistan and has lived in Tashkent region for 26 years. Another applicant, Robiya Qahhorova, waited 40 years for citizenship. Since 2016, nearly 26,000 people have been granted citizenship.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Four Years for Fighting in Ukraine
item.description: A 19-year-old Uzbek citizen who fought for Russia in the Ukraine conflict has been sentenced to four years in prison by a court in Uzbekistan's Samarqand region. He had traveled to Vladivostok for work and was imprisoned for drug offenses. While serving his sentence, he signed a contract with the Russian Ministry of Defense to fight in Ukraine in exchange for early release and other benefits.

item.title: Man Suspected of Molesting Nine-Year-Old Girl in Almaty Region
item.description: Police in the Almaty region are investigating a case of alleged molestation of a nine-year-old girl in the village of Irgeli. Local residents reported that a man allegedly took the child to a store, bought her sweets, and then began to harass her. A criminal case has been registered, and a final procedural decision will be made after an examination.

item.title: Kazakhstan launches 'Umai' mortgage program for women with 15% down payment
item.description: Kazakh women can apply for the 'Umai' housing program starting August 31. The maximum loan is 50 million tenge, with a down payment of 15-20%. The program offers an annual interest rate of 14.8%. The Asian Development Bank has provided nine billion tenge for the first phase. Eligible women must have at least six months of official income and a family's average monthly net income not exceeding 1.25 million tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan to introduce personal interest declarations for civil servants in 2027
item.description: Starting in 2027, civil servants in Kazakhstan will be required to submit declarations of personal interests within 15 working days of assuming their roles. This applies to individuals in responsible state positions and those authorized to perform state functions. The declaration will include information on participation in commercial organizations and individual entrepreneurship, even up to a year before taking office.

item.title: Former MP Tokon Mamytov Denies Signing 'Letter of 75'
item.description: Former member of parliament Tokon Mamytov denied signing the 'Letter of 75' during court proceedings in Bishkek. The letter, signed by 75 individuals including former officials and cultural figures, urged President Sadyr Japarov to schedule presidential elections for 2026 instead of January 2027. Mamytov stated he did not sign the document.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva discusses railway, governance, and economic cooperation with China's Wang Yi
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing. They discussed Uzbekistan's interest in learning from China's governance experience, particularly in poverty reduction, and deepening cooperation in agriculture, science, education, and the digital economy. The China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project was also discussed.

item.title: Tashkent to Launch $288 Million DP World Logistics Hub in October
item.description: Tashkent plans to attract $9 billion in investments by the end of 2026, according to Mayor Shavkat Umurzakov. A key project is the DP World logistics hub, with construction set to begin in October. The hub will be designed to handle 120 million tons of cargo and 150,000 containers. Tashkent was ranked third among the world's fastest-growing cities by Boston Consulting Group.

item.title: Astana Court Hears Testimony on Paramedic's Death, Possibility of Faster Response
item.description: The Inter-District Criminal Court in Astana continued the trial regarding the death of paramedic Uldana Myrzuan. A senior paramedic from the medical team present on the day of the incident testified, along with the head of the emergency department. The prosecution requested to question another paramedic, Aktymak Sizdykova, who reportedly provided assistance to the deceased. The defense objected, but the judge granted the request.

item.title: Wall Painting from 4th-5th Century Discovered at Boburtepa Archaeological Site
item.description: Archaeological excavations at the Boburtepa site in Uzbekistan's Qashqadaryo region have uncovered remnants of an ancient building and a unique wall painting. The artwork, depicting tulips and white flowers with red wavy lines, was found on a western wall and dates back to the 4th-5th centuries AD. Experts suggest the structure may have been a temple.

item.title: Suspects Detained for Brutal Attack on Woman in Turkistan Region
item.description: Two men have been detained in connection with a brutal attack on a woman in the Turkistan region of Kazakhstan. The suspects allegedly broke into the woman's home, assaulted her, and stole her mobile phone. A criminal case has been initiated, and police are investigating the circumstances of the incident.
